title: Hundreds of websites deliver potent malware cocktail to unsuspecting visitors
gist: Attackers injected malicious code into Optimizely-signed JavaScript served from cdn.optimizely.com, infecting 178 identified customer sites (including CNN, Zoom, the BBC and Salesforce; the title says 'hundreds') with a payload that swapped crypto wallet addresses, skimmed cards, stole cookies/screenshots and delivered Coruna and DarkSword iOS exploit kits. How the attackers gained cross-customer write access is unknown.

insights.claim: ReportURI identified 178 websites, including CNN, Zoom, the BBC, and Salesforce, that served malicious JavaScript through the Optimizely personalization platform.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Third-party script supply chains are a systemic web security risk; Optimizely faces customer trust and liability fallout.

insights.claim: The attack was not CDN cache poisoning but used Optimizely's legitimate infrastructure, with tainted code delivered from cdn.optimizely.com under a valid certificate, also affecting Optimizely's own www and login pages.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Signed, trusted vendor code can be weaponized; demand for client-side script monitoring may rise.

insights.claim: It is unknown how attackers gained write access to so many unrelated customer projects, whether via a compromised Optimizely system or a credential with cross-customer access, and Optimizely did not respond.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Root cause disclosure will determine Optimizely's reputational damage.
insights.quote: “We don’t know how the attacker got write access to so many unrelated customer projects

insights.claim: The malicious track.js swapped wallet addresses for nine cryptocurrencies with the attacker's, and ReportURI said funds have already been stolen.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Crypto users face clipboard/address-swap risk from mainstream websites.

insights.claim: The script skimmed card numbers, expiry dates, and CVVs from HTTP requests, but cards entered in hosted payment iframes such as Stripe and Adyen were unaffected.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Hosted payment iframes proved protective, a selling point for Stripe/Adyen-style integrations.

insights.claim: The attack delivered iOS exploit kits Coruna, targeting iOS 13 to 17, and DarkSword, targeting iOS 18.x, via a hidden iframe, while a chain for iOS 26 only fingerprints devices.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Older iOS versions remain exploitable; update adoption matters for Apple device security.

insights.claim: Earlier this month, hackers possibly linked to the Kremlin attempted to deliver DarkSword through multiple vectors, including a compromised web analytics service.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Possible state-linked activity raises the stakes of web analytics supply-chain attacks.

insights.claim: There is no information yet on how successful the exploit chains were, and the list of 178 sites may not be exhaustive.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Impact scope may grow as researchers investigate.
insights.locator: At the moment, there’s no information
